sources.note: Abaga mentioned only on p. 472 (as 'the Abaga language of the Finisterre Stock.. shares 25%-30% basic vocabulary cognates with Kamano, and is structurally quite similar to it, except for some features of its verb structure'). The East-Central Family note (p. ~478: 'a strong development of supra-segmental features manifesting themselves in tonal systems and combined tone-stress systems') is about Kamano/Gahuku-subfamily languages; Wurm placed Abaga outside that family, so no statement about Abaga stress or tone.
